$description: Trellis token source, in the W3C Design Tokens format. One seed for every platform: lengths are in cells or in points, never in rem or px. A point is one CSS pixel at the reader's default text size, one pt on iOS, one dp on Android. tools/build-tokens.js writes the generated tokens of core.css from this file, and does the rem conversion for the web. Formulas (the fit, the ratio, the gutter) are not values and are not here: see math.js.

cell.$description: The cell, the measure of space. Its target grows in a straight line from the narrow screen to the wide one, then holds, and it follows the reader's text size.

target-narrow.$description: The cell on a narrow screen.

target-wide.$description: The cell on a wide screen.

screen-narrow.$description: Up to this width the cell is target-narrow.

screen-wide.$description: From this width the cell is target-wide.

text-scale-max.$description: The cap on the cell: it follows the reader's text size up to this many times the default, and no further. Above it only type grows, and layouts reflow.

frame.$description: The page's outer box, in cells.

space.$description: The named counts: space, counted in cells. Any whole count is on the grid and no set of counts is enforced; these are the ones with names. Between blocks, space is whole cells; halves and quarters live inside things.

q.$description: A quarter cell, rounded to a whole pixel and never less than a line.

13.$description: With 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8, the Fibonacci counts: a set that suits a golden type ratio.

size.$description: Named sizes, each in cells, or in cells plus a line.

base.$description: One cell plus a line each side.

hit-min.$description: The least hit area on a coarse pointer, whatever a control draws. A platform layer turns this: 44 on iOS, 48 on Android.

control-type.$description: Control labels: fixed sizes, not fluid. The only font sizes outside the type roles.

radius.$description: Corners are measured in cells too. A nested corner is the outer corner less the padding.

layer.$description: One scale for everything that stacks.

type.$description: The ratio's neutral defaults. Two anchors, H1 and body, each with a size in a narrow space and a wide one; headings step down from H1 by one ratio and paragraphs step out from body by another, and both ratios open with the space. A product layer turns all of these.

color.$description: A relational palette: one seed, the accent, the other seeds derived from it, and every role derived from a seed. A product sets the accent, may set any other seed, and may turn the lift, the flip and the gradient settings; it never sets a role. Seeds are OKLCH, each in its light-theme form. math.js derives every seed and role from these in arithmetic; core.css does it with relative colors.

seed.$description: One color, in its light-theme form: the accent. The other nine seeds follow from it (see derive): the neutral, the five kinds (what sort of thing this is; shape and color both follow kind; topic is also the default tag) and the three statuses. A product may set any of them in its place.

accent.$description: The primary action, and the focus ring.

derive.$description: How the other seeds follow from the accent, in arithmetic that core.css states with relative colors and math.js repeats. A kind is the accent turned around the hue wheel; a status keeps its own hue and takes the accent's strength; the neutral takes the accent's hue and a trace of chroma. Each takes the accent's lightness, kept clear of the ink flip so its ink reads at 4.5:1, and no more chroma than sRGB holds at its hue.

clear-below.$description: A derived seed whose ink is white is no lighter than this.

clear-above.$description: A derived seed whose ink is dark is no darker than this. The dark theme lifts a seed, so one whose ink is white is also no darker than this less the lift.

kind-chroma.$description: A kind's chroma, as a share of the accent's.

kind-turn.$description: How far each kind is turned from the accent: a fifth of the wheel apart. Topic is not turned.

topic-step.$description: Topic is the accent, this much darker.

status-chroma.$description: A status's chroma, as a share of the accent's.

status-chroma-min.$description: And never less than this, so a status reads under a quiet accent.

status.$description: Each status's own hue, and the most chroma sRGB holds there for each unit of lightness.

neutral-chroma.$description: The neutral's chroma: a trace of the accent's hue.

limit.$description: The most chroma sRGB holds at a hue, for each unit of lightness, as two waves around the hue wheel: base + wave × cos(hue − wave-at) + wave-two × cos(2 × (hue − wave-two-at)). It runs under the real limit at every hue for a seed whose ink is white.

lift.$description: How much lighter a hue is in the dark theme, in OKLCH lightness.

ink-flip.$description: Ink on a fill: white on a fill darker than this lightness, a dark ink of the fill's own hue on a lighter one.

neutral.$description: Neutral roles: the neutral seed's hue and chroma at a lightness for each theme.

bg-raised-2.$description: A surface on a surface: a step back toward the page in light, a step lighter in dark.

gradient.$description: A gradient is an interpolation space and its stops, from roles; the author adds a direction or a shape.

turn.$description: How far the accent gradient turns its hue, in degrees.
